message:
fix(lk-ux-retry r2): one deadline for the whole retry; the earlier wait's end kept apart from the new password's fate

Codex SOURCE NEEDS_CHANGES on 9991b36 (codex_lk_ux_retry_src_r1.md):

N1 -- a retry whose caller had already answered 18 could still supersede the earlier wait and take a fresh
challenge and hold. Now the retry carries one absolute deadline (a little inside the caller's wait): at the
caller's timeout a retry not started is taken off the queue and its transaction withdrawn; the worker checks
'still owned and in time' before the supersede and again before the fresh challenge, and each exchange waits
only to the deadline. A supersede that did complete leaves the earlier request its own end (17), and the retry
is answered 17 with no challenge and no hold.

N2 -- the viewer took 'not 0 and not 18' to mean the earlier wait ended, and turned a later Superseded into
'not confirmed in 2 minutes'. Now the earlier wait is over exactly when the retry's challenge was issued (or the
retry was answered 17); a new password that then fails before sealing / gets no answer is said as that
(kLockRetryNotSent / kLockRetryUnknown), and a Superseded is never shown as the 2-minute timeout.

The protocol comments now say the numbers are assigned by the verifier (89, 0x80000, 17/18, IPC 9, 0x2).

Tests: relay ondemand 70/70 x5 (N1 counterexamples: withdrawn before start, supersede past the deadline,
challenge past the deadline after a supersede, EndSession during the supersede); e2e --lock-screen 62/62 with
the N2 counterexample (a sealing failure after the retry's challenge -- REMOTE60_VIEWER_UNLOCK_TEST_SEAM, defined
for that e2e target only); prelogin 79/79, not-prelogin 28/28, lockcred 72/72, service 12/12. Mutants: N1
reverted -> 5 FAIL (a supersede and a challenge after 18); N2 reverted -> 3 FAIL (the '2 minutes' text).
